The fixture exposes only its own test interface `mir5-library-native-input`: `report` reads observations without initializing or changing state; `advance` accepts only the fixed step names below and cannot substitute for the specified native input. The private governor-owned caller must check the exact phase, read real client PID/start/engine/window identities, freeze each actor spec, send the declared input, then validate the resulting native GUI/event/world observation. The new [input actor](../../../tools/Invoke-LibraryNativeInput.ps1) reuses the existing owned-window checks and Windows `SendInput`; it creates or closes no Factorio process and has no save, archive or release authority. A successful input-send receipt alone is never a gameplay result.

`inspect` and each later private probe require empty private results/details and disabled native-open actions while retaining all imported native levels/flags/effects. Before the cold-host private probe, the fixture first verifies both already restored personal queries and the dragged location without opening either Library. The completed sequence has48 private queries, five actual joins, two keyboard-close events, at least one drag event, two requested native resets and one actual removal of the newly joined German test player. It never creates a fake player. Its two new saves are `mir5-library-native-input-restart` and `mir5-library-native-input-complete`. Keep owned native screenshots and actor receipts separately for every action and both final clients.

Black Glass must still bind/review the private caller, exact five-mod profiles, protected source/corrected historical fixture members, actual archive hashes, desktop points, ordered actor/readback commands, closed-save custody, clients-first teardown and restoration before executing.
